sentences.text: The genus Venustodus includes six known species: V. argutus, V. leidyi, V. robustus, V. tenuicristatus, V. variabilis, and V. venustus.
The genus Venustodus was first described by St. John and Worthen in 1875.
The type species of the genus Venustodus is Venustodus venustus — the species the genus is based on.
All species of Venustodus were believed to be nektonic marine carnivores.
Venustodus is classified either in the family Cochliodontidae or has an indeterminate position within the subclass Holocephali.
In 1984, researcher Rainer Zangerl suggested that the classification of Venustodus was unknown and that it might not be related to holocephalans.
The parent group of Venustodus is the family Cochliodontidae.
Venustodus lived during the Carboniferous period in Russia and the United States.
Venustodus lived from the Visean to the Moscovian stages, approximately 346.7 to 307 million years ago.
